To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a genetic iPL(2)-VIB deficiency in mice is accompanied by reduced DHA metabolism and profound changes in lipid metabolizing enzyme expression and in the phospholipid content of brain (especially of DHA).
iPLA(β) is required for normal brain metabolism and function, and that its deficiency causes a profound disturbance of brain phospholipase and fatty acid metabolism.

understanding the role of calcium-independent phospholipoase A2 (iPLA2) in the brain, which is the major site of docosahexanoic acid (DHa) synthesis in the body.
the metabolism of the polyunsaturated fatty acids in the brain and the role they play in the development and function of the brain.
understanding the role of calcium-independent phospholipes A(2) (iPLA2) in brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
iPLA2β plays a key role in brain phospholipo- and docosah- hexaenoic acid homeostasis.

the iPLA2β gene is a critical regulator of DHA metabolism and that the absence of iPLA2beta in mice leads to changes in DHA metabolism that may contribute to the neurologic abnormalities in patients with PLA2G mutations.
the iPLA2β knockout mouse model is a good model for studying the function of the enzyme and that the results are consistent with a role for iPLA2 in DHA metabolism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
iPLA(β) is a key enzyme in the DHA metabolism and its deficiency leads to a profound change in brain DHA metabolism and lipid metabolism.

iPLA( 2β) is a major DHA phospholipid hydrolase in mouse brain, and that iPLA (2β) is important for maintaining normal phospholipid DHA content and turnover, and normal phospholipase and cyclooxygenase enzyme expression in brain.
iPLA( 2)β is the major enzyme responsible for the release of DHA from phospholipid in vivo, and that it is the only enzyme that can do so.
The main takeaway from our work is that
iPLA( 2)β plays an essential role in the brain by regulating DHA metabolism and lipid-metabolism enzymes.
the brain is highly dependent on iPLA2β for its phospholipid remodeling, and that iPLA2γ and sPLA2-V may not compensate for the lack of iPLA2b.
iPLA( 2)β is a critical enzyme for DHA metabolism and brain phospholipases in general.
